 JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - The National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) has urged the public to heightened vigilance against potential hydrometeorological disasters as the rainy season begins in November 2026.
 Acting Head of the Data, Information, and Disaster Communication Center at BNPB, Berton Panjaitan, reminded the public of various potential disasters, including floods, landslides, strong winds, and tornadoes.
 "We will continue to issue warnings regarding hydrometeorological hazards so that all parties, including local governments, volunteers, and the public, can prepare for floods," Berton stated during a press conference at the BNPB Studio on Tuesday (3/11/2026).
 Berton noted that the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) has issued weather warnings for several regions in Indonesia, particularly for November 4, 2026.
 "BMKG has issued a warning for the weather in Indonesia, especially for November 4," he said.
 Regions likely to experience moderate rainfall include Aceh, North Sumatra, West Sumatra, Riau, Jambi, Bengkulu, South Sumatra, West Kalimantan, Papua, Central Papua, and the Papua Mountains.
 In light of the potential disasters, BNPB has called on local governments, volunteers, and the community to increase preparedness.
 One of the necessary steps is to clean drainage channels communally to reduce flood risks.
 The public is also urged to familiarize themselves with evacuation routes and prepare disaster emergency kits to sustain basic needs for at least three days.
 "Preparing an emergency kit that can last for at least three days is crucial," Berton emphasized.
 Additionally, individuals are encouraged to inspect infrastructure conditions, including dams, and to conduct river monitoring with the assistance of competent personnel.
 To prepare for strong winds and tornadoes, BNPB has advised the community to reinforce roof structures and trim branches and trees that may pose a falling hazard.
 Residents are also encouraged to avoid billboards and trees during high winds due to the risk of collapse.
 People living in landslide-prone areas should evacuate immediately if heavy rain persists for an extended period.
 Residents must also recognize signs of landslides, such as the appearance of cracks in the ground or on building floors.
